texts: Whenever wind reflects off harbor water at a harbor lantern, that lantern burns its mire-essence quickly.

(: whenever_reflect_burn (Implication (And (Member $e reflect) (Patient $e wind) (Source $e harbor_water) (Location $e $y) (Member $y harbor_lantern)) (And (Member (sk_burn $e) burn) (Agent (sk_burn $e) $y) (Patient (sk_burn $e) (sk_mire_essence $y)) (Member (sk_mire_essence $y) mire_essence) (Possession (sk_mire_essence $y) $y) (Manner (sk_burn $e) quickly) (During (sk_burn $e) $e))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

good. the whenever-clause becomes a rule that can actually fire: the trigger is one finite clause whose participants (wind, harbor water, the lantern it happens at) are all ordinary matchable terms, so a later sentence reporting such a reflection sets off the burning. "that lantern" is correctly tied back to the lantern the reflection happened at, and the burning keeps the possessed mire-essence, the "quickly" manner and its simultaneity with the trigger.
No wraith has emerged in the past twenty-six years.

good. the explicit "no" lands as a blanket denial over wraiths with the quantifier word itself recorded, the perfect "has emerged" as plain past, and "in the past twenty-six years" as a backward window on the emergence rather than a claim that an emerging lasted twenty-six years.
Together, the displaced nightmoths keep the lanterns at the Hollows productive.

good. "Together" is read as one joint keeping by the moth group rather than a separate act per moth, "displaced" is handed down to each moth individually instead of being pinned on the group as a whole, and the lanterns are placed at the Hollows as a named location. The maintenance sense of "keep" is preserved too: the lanterns' productive state is recorded as continuing and as the result of the keeping, with each lantern individually productive.
Wraiths that are in the Sunken Cove sometimes harm sky-cats.

good. the relative clause becomes a fireable condition (a wraith that is located in the Sunken Cove), each such wraith gets its own harming of sky-cats, and 'sometimes' is carried both as the rule's strength and as the recorded quantifier word; the named cove and the sky-cat kind both keep their kind links, so nothing in the sentence is dropped.
Whenever a tide-pool stone is submerged, salt-bloom grows on that stone.

good. the whenever-clause becomes a fireable per-occurrence rule: every submerging of a tide-pool stone yields its own growing of salt-bloom, located on that same stone and tied to that occasion, and both hyphenated compounds keep their kind links.
The distillation yield thins throughout deep winter.

mixed: the thinning, its subject and both compounds parse fine, but 'throughout deep winter' is recorded as a during-link that treats the season as if it were a second event, so the season never reaches the event's ordinary time slot and a later 'when does the yield thin?' question cannot find it; the continuous-span sense of 'throughout' is lost either way. Rewrite as: 'The distillation yield thins in deep winter.' — the season then lands in the time slot where it is queryable, and nothing the current parse actually records is given up.
The moth-count declines throughout late autumn.

mixed: the decline and its late-autumn frame both land, but the count is filed as something the declining physically changes rather than as the value that moves (the shape a 'what fell, and by how much' question matches), and 'moth-count' fuses into one opaque symbol, so 'a count of what?' cannot be answered from the record. Rewrite as 'The count of moths falls throughout late autumn.' - 'falls' is one of the verbs the translator reads as a change of value, and 'count of moths' exposes moths as the thing being counted. Separately, a bare season has no time slot of its own, so 'late autumn' is filed as though it were another event and the whole-span sense of 'throughout' is lost either way; naming a month ('in November') is the only wording with a real calendar slot, so use it only if that is what the rule actually means.
Whenever a new year begins, the Council begins a new ledger.

(: yearly_ledger_rule (Implication (And (Member $e begin) (Patient $e $y) (Member $y year) (Member $y new)) (And (Member (sk_begin_ledger $e) begin) (Agent (sk_begin_ledger $e) sk_council_1) (Patient (sk_begin_ledger $e) (sk_ledger $e)) (Member (sk_ledger $e) ledger) (Member (sk_ledger $e) new) (During (sk_begin_ledger $e) $e))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

good. the 'whenever' clause becomes a fireable rule - every new-year beginning triggers a Council ledger-opening tied to that occurrence, with a fresh new ledger minted per year and all participants covered.
